assessment.nobel_worthiness: A clean continuum model predicted that flat bands appear at a magic twist angle, and experiment then found correlated insulators and superconductivity there. This is the kind of simple, general mechanism that opened a whole field (moire quantum matter, twistronics). The theory is analytically transparent and was tested directly against experiment.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald theory of 2011 and the Jarillo-Herrero group's 2018 experiments are the decisive pair. This gives a natural theory-plus-experiment configuration. Credit for earlier twisted-bilayer theory (e.g. Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) and for contemporaneous experiments by other groups is not captured in the supplied names, and a fair three-way split is somewhat contested.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced in many laboratories over several years. The field is still moving fast, but the central discovery of flat-band-driven correlated states is firmly established. Recognition now seems timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: The origin of the superconductivity (pairing mechanism) remains unsettled.
Whether the prize should tie the discovery to one experiment group or to the broader moire platform.
I have not independently verified the details of the priority claims for earlier theory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Vicsek model and the Toner-Tu hydrodynamic theory show how a minimal non-equilibrium rule produces long-range order in two dimensions, in apparent defiance of Mermin-Wagner. The result is a universal mechanism, analysed with the tools of statistical physics (renormalisation group, hydrodynamics). It founded modern active matter and links to biology, soft matter and collective behaviour.
assessment.attribution: Vicsek introduced the minimal flocking model (1995). Toner and Tu gave the continuum theory and the exact scaling arguments. Ramaswamy contributed key early hydrodynamics of active fluids (Simha-Ramaswamy, with Pierre-Gilles de Gennes' school in the background). The supplied three names give a reasonable configuration, although Yuhai Tu is not credited here, and that omission may be unfair to the theory.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of confirmation through simulations, colloidal and vibrated-granular experiments, and bacterial and cell collectives. Quantitative tests of the Toner-Tu exponents in experiments are still limited, but the concept is stable and widely accepted.
uncertainties: Direct experimental validation of the predicted exponents is limited.
Priority among Vicsek, Toner-Tu and the Ramaswamy school depends on which element (model versus theory versus hydrodynamics) is rewarded.
Yuhai Tu is absent from the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Z2 topological insulator and quantum spin Hall effect (Kane-Mele, 2005) turned topological band theory into a broadly applicable classification, and the HgTe experiment of Molenkamp's group gave a decisive realisation. It is a simple model with a deep general idea, and is highly influential across condensed-matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the key theoretical proposal. Molenkamp led the first experimental observation in HgTe wells (Konig et al., 2007), following a prediction by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, who are not credited in the supplied names. Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang is an unresolved credit question for the three-person configuration. The three names offered are still a coherent core.
assessment.maturity: Very mature. Many materials, transport and ARPES confirmations, and a well-understood interpretation. The 2016 prize on topological phase transitions covered a related, earlier strand, so overlap would need to be handled in the citation.
uncertainties: Relation to the 2016 Nobel Prize (Thouless, Haldane, Kosterlitz) and how much novelty it leaves.
Credit for the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and for the three-dimensional generalisation.
Whether the supplied credit is the best one for a single prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KPZ equation defined a universality class of non-equilibrium growth with exact exponents and, later, exact distributions linked to random-matrix (Tracy-Widom) statistics. It is exactly the sort of surprising universality that statistical physics values, and it connects to integrable probability, turbulence-adjacent models and experiments on liquid-crystal turbulence.
assessment.attribution: Kardar, Parisi and Zhang wrote the 1986 paper. Parisi is not among the supplied names, and he already has a prize (2021), but this is a genuine credit complication. The exact solutions are due to Spohn, Prahofer, Sasamoto, Amir-Corwin-Quastel and others, so the 'decisive' contributions split between model creation and exact solution.
assessment.maturity: Strong theoretical maturity. Experimental confirmation (Takeuchi-Sano liquid-crystal experiments) of the Tracy-Widom statistics is real but limited to a few systems, and the broad significance in real surface growth is still discussed.
uncertainties: Omission of Giorgio Parisi from the credited names makes a fair allocation hard.
Whether the prize would reward the 1986 equation or the later exact solutions.
Breadth of experimental evidence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation of Hubbard-type models with cold atoms (superfluid to Mott insulator, Fermi-Hubbard physics, quantum gas microscopy) lets one realise clean models from statistical physics and study them directly. It is a conceptually clean programme with clear impact on many-body physics, close to the viewpoint of a theorist who likes simple model systems.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch) proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation. Greiner et al. 2002 observed the Mott transition, and Bloch led the broad programme including microscopy and many-body control. Esslinger's fermionic experiments are also decisive, and the choice of three out of four credited names is a real allocation problem. Cold-atom physics already has the 1997 and 2001 prizes.
assessment.maturity: Mature in techniques and widely replicated. The ultimate scientific payoff (answers to open problems such as the Fermi-Hubbard phase diagram) is still developing, which makes timing arguable.
uncertainties: Choice among Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger and Zoller.
Whether quantum simulation has yet solved a problem unreachable by other methods.
Overlap with previous cold-atom prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming picture explains rigidity onset in disordered packings through isostaticity, critical scaling and a universal set of exponents, and the idea has a simple mechanism that makes quantitative predictions. It unified granular matter, foams, emulsions and glasses. It is a strong example of universality in soft matter.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel proposed the jamming phase diagram (1998) and O'Hern, Silbert, Liu and Nagel gave the numerical point-J analysis. Wyart developed the isostaticity and marginal-stability theory. The supplied credits are reasonable, although the numerical contributions of O'Hern and Silbert and the mean-field theory of Parisi, Zamponi and others are not covered.
assessment.maturity: Considerable confirmation in simulation and in granular and colloidal experiments, but the connection to the glass transition and to infinite-dimensional mean-field theory is still being clarified. Interpretation is not yet fully stable.
uncertainties: Whether the jamming transition is a true critical point or is controlled by protocol.
Relation to the mean-field theory of the glass and jamming transitions.
Credit for O'Hern and Silbert, who are not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution (BB84, E91) is a clear conceptual invention that turns a basic feature of quantum mechanics (no-cloning, entanglement) into a technology, with real deployments. The ideas are simple and general, and the link to Bell-test physics makes it a physics rather than purely computer-science contribution.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard (BB84) are the clear originators. Ekert's 1991 entanglement-based protocol is an independent and important contribution, with Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea in the background. A three-person configuration is plausible, but Wiesner is not credited and has died.
assessment.maturity: Decades of experimental implementation and security proofs. Practical security (device imperfections, side channels) remains a topic, but the foundational principle is settled. The 2022 prize on entanglement and Bell tests (Aspect, Clauser, Zeilinger) is closely related, which may reduce the novelty.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 Nobel Prize on Bell tests and quantum information.
Priority issues with Wiesner.
Practical impact of QKD is still debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1984 BPZ work on conformal field theory gave exact solutions of two-dimensional critical phenomena, with universal exponents, and shaped statistical physics, string theory and later conformal bootstrap methods. It is the definitive example of an exactly solvable universality framework.
assessment.attribution: Belavin, Polyakov and Zamolodchikov are the authors of the central paper. Zamolodchikov died in 2025 (I am not fully certain of the date), which would complicate a prize, and the credited names omit Friedan, Qiu and Shenker, Cardy and Dotsenko-Fateev. The three-name set is natural but the allocation is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and thoroughly confirmed in theory and in numerical checks of 2D critical systems (e.g. Ising and Potts), but it is chiefly a theoretical framework with limited direct experimental test, and it is very old, which raises the question of timeliness.
uncertainties: Possible death of a key laureate.
Omitted contributors (Cardy, Friedan, Dotsenko-Fateev).
Whether the committee favours a theory without a decisive experimental event.
